description: One extractor feeds a barracks through a five-cell conduit; buffers drained each tick.
A splitter alternates between a direct barracks and a barracks two cells away; drained.
Two sources of the same resource join in a merger feeding a turret; drained.

A merger fed directly by another merger (and so by an extractor) and, through a 5-cell conduit, by a second extractor, behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: both inputs are always backed up and the merger alternates between them (each branch gets 60 of the 120 items consumed, give or take the items in flight) instead of always taking the conduit.
A crossover carries two resources through each other to a turret and an overclocker; drained.
A splitter with no output conduit: every item is lost.
Buffers are never drained: the buffer fills, the conduit fills, the source stalls, nothing is lost.

A merger fed directly by two extractors (no conduits), behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: both sources are always ready, so the merger's round-robin pointer, not the building ID, decides who fills the cell and the two extractors alternate (each ends with about half of the items produced) instead of the lower ID monopolising it.

A merger fed directly by one extractor and, through a 5-cell conduit, by a second one, behind a barracks that takes one unit per 25 ticks: the direct source counts as ready when it would produce this tick, so the merger alternates between it and the conduit instead of always taking the conduit.

Drained: a slow direct extractor (tier 1, one item per 20 ticks) and a fast one (tier 3, one per 10 ticks) behind a 10-cell conduit feed a merger. On the tick the conduit's item reaches its last cell, the direct extractor has a countdown of 1 and would produce: it counts as ready, so the merger's round-robin pointer (which favours the direct input) lets it fill the cell and the conduit item waits one tick. If a source were ready only at countdown 0, the conduit would win that tick and the slow extractor would lose a tick (19 items instead of 20).
A tier 3 collector (100 per 1000 ticks) feeds a splitter with two tier 1 barracks (each needs 75): both are under-supplied and get an even split (PP-7).

A tier 3 and a tier 2 collector (171 per 1000 ticks) feed a merger and a splitter with a tier 1 barracks (needs 75) and a tier 3 barracks (needs 100). The even share (85) is above the tier 1 barracks' top speed: its production interval, not its store, makes that path back up, and the tier 3 barracks takes the remainder.
The same supply (171 per 1000 ticks) into two tier 1 barracks (75 each): both reach their top speed, both paths back up and the collectors stall; nothing is lost.
A three-way splitter with the east output unconnected: the two connected tier 1 barracks (north, west) share the items evenly; the unconnected output is skipped, nothing is lost.
